title: I am officially obese (Hypertrophy Log #7)
summary: A home basement gym log with an upper day (pronated-grip curls on a 1970s bar, power flies, serratus push-ups, lying triceps extensions, belt-squat rows, steep preacher curls) and a lower day (SSB reverse lunges, tibialis machine, belt-squat RDLs with rest-pause, neck). He then explains his two-month absence: losing and fighting to regain his job, stress-induced high blood pressure, a clinically 'obese' BMI of 30, and plans for weekly Saturday streams from September.
claims: Curling against a wall reduces cheating and allows slower negatives
Keep negatives very slow; he says the negative is where most hypertrophy occurs
Power flies (between press and fly, dumbbells rotated outward, elbows flared) let you lift more than flies and stretch deeply; keep the weight light
In a superset or giant set, not every exercise can be maximally intense; serratus push-ups are a low-intensity finisher for shoulder health
A lying triceps extension with a pullover motion, using a pronated-grip bar, gives a better top squeeze and spares wrists and elbows
Rows on the belt squat machine let the machine handle stability so you can push traps hard; tilt the head away for more stretch
The stretch at the bottom matters most for back training; pulling all the way back can be counterproductive
Machines let you train hard by offloading stability
Dumbbell preacher curls on a hyperextension bench give a steeper angle, keeping stress on the muscle instead of the tendon
Life doesn't need to be perfectly regimented to look good; sticking to training and progressing is enough
Reverse lunges with an SSB destroy the glutes more than anything and spare the lower back; hold supports only for balance
Eliminating balance demands improves split squats and similar lifts
He trains tibialis on a machine every lower day, now 50 lb per foot for sets of 20; three times a week makes a big difference
Belt-squat RDLs remove stability so you just hinge; finish with rest-pause using 15-second breaks
For the front of the neck pure isolation is best; for the back of the neck some torso movement feels more natural
Train your neck as much as possible: it pays off in facial and body aesthetics and protects you in accidents
He lost his job three months earlier and fought a litigious termination until getting it back
His BMI of 30 labelled him clinically obese, surprising the doctor who saw him
Stress from the job dispute caused high blood pressure and other health complications
He didn't skip a single gym day during the crisis; bodybuilding kept him together mentally
He plans weekly three-hour Saturday streams from September, free for everyone

more load than flies, better stretch
bring arms slightly forward at top
triceps long head squeeze, joint friendly
tilt head away, emphasize bottom stretch
traps and upper back with external stability
